sources: A six-coefficient affine geotransform maps pixel/line coordinates to georeferenced coordinates.
GT(0),GT(3) identify the upper-left corner of the upper-left pixel.
The center of the top-left pixel is pixel/line coordinate (0.5,0.5).
Raster pixel/line coordinates run from (0,0) at the upper-left corner to (width,height) at the lower-right corner.
For north-up rasters GT(1) is pixel width and GT(2) is zero.
For north-up rasters GT(5) is pixel height, normally negative, and GT(4) is zero.
GDAL raster data model treats affine geotransform as the common pixel/line-to-world mapping.
GDAL raster data model corner convention
The geotransform origin is the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, not its center.
GDAL raster data model center offset
Pixel center addressing requires a half-pixel offset from integer corner coordinates.
GDALApplyGeoTransform applies the six coefficients to fractional pixel/line coordinates.
GDALInvGeoTransform inverts a standard 3x2 geotransform and reports failure if uninvertible.
GDALComposeGeoTransforms composes two geotransforms into an equivalent transform.
GCP-to-geotransform fitting can introduce small rotation terms from calculation imprecision.
GCP-to-geotransform supports approximate fitting and configurable pixel-error threshold, so terminal exact affine provenance must reject unpinned approximation.
Python ApplyGeoTransform accepts fractional column/row positions with zero at the left/top edge.
Python InvGeoTransform converts world coordinates back to fractional image column/row.
Applying an inverse transform to a transformed pixel/line location can recover the original fractional image coordinate.
GDALGeoTransform GetInverse returns false when the transform is uninvertible.
GDALGeoTransform can report whether rotation terms are absent through IsAxisAligned.
Rescale changes scale and rotation terms and is typically used for overview transforms, so native terminal addressing must not inherit overview scaling.
gdaltransform supports inverse coordinate transformation with -i.
gdaltransform supports source and target coordinate epochs for dynamic-CRS transformations.
A custom coordinate operation must account for source and target axis order.
-a_gt overrides output geotransform metadata without reprojection.
Assigning output nodata metadata does not rewrite source pixels equal to the old nodata value.
GDAL driver geotransforms are anchored at the top-left corner rather than pixel center.
GeoTIFF RasterPixelIsPoint represents a point sample rather than an area sample.
RasterPixelIsArea is the default area-based pixel interpretation.
PixelIsPoint tie-point interpretation requires a half-pixel offset into GDAL's area-based georeferencing model.
AREA_OR_POINT controls GeoTIFF point/area metadata while GDAL geotransform extents remain area-based.
World files use an area-based pixel assumption but store the origin at the center of the top-left pixel.
Rasterio rowcol/index defaults to numpy.floor for fractional image coordinates.
Rasterio rowcol permits floor, ceiling, round, or another explicit operation, so terminal mapping must pin the operation.
Rasterio xy returns pixel center coordinates by default.
Rasterio xy can explicitly return ul, ur, ll, or lr pixel corners.
Rasterio index returns the row and column of the pixel containing an x,y coordinate.
array_bounds derives west,south,east,north from height,width and affine transform.
from_bounds derives an affine transform from exact bounds and raster dimensions.
from_origin derives an affine transform from upper-left coordinates and pixel sizes.
Rasterio image columns increase rightward and rows increase downward from the upper-left.
AffineTransformer xy and rowcol provide forward and inverse raster/world coordinate conversion.
Rasterio Window offsets and lengths are floats in its float-precision window model.
Window row/column indexes are defined relative to the upper-left of the dataset.
Window.round can remove tiny floating-point artifacts from computed windows.
round_offsets rounds row/column offsets to the preceding whole number.
round_lengths rounds window width and height to the nearest whole number without changing offsets.
window_index rounds starting indexes down and stopping indexes up.
from_bounds maps geospatial bounds to a potentially floating-point raster window.
window_bounds returns geospatial bounds for a dataset window.
window_transform returns an affine transform local to a dataset window.
Window evaluation treats negative indexes differently when boundless mode is enabled.
Raster clip preserves original resolution and rounds bounds to whole pixel locations without resampling.
Bounding-box clip expands bounds when necessary to match input pixel boundaries.
--window uses column,line,width,height pixel coordinates measured from the left and top.
Window/bbox regions outside the source can be filled with zero when no nodata exists, so terminal reads must reject such fill.
GDAL raster clip geometry overlap rule
Geometry clipping selects all pixels overlapping the geometry, distinct from center-in-polygon semantics.
-tap aligns raster extent coordinates to integer multiples of target resolution.
-tr explicitly sets positive x/y target resolution.
Rasterize output defaults to Float64 unless the burn field is Int64 and supported.
The transform precision parameter is unused/deprecated; deterministic behavior must not depend on it.
The windows precision parameter is unused/deprecated; explicit rounding policy is required.
An uninvertible geotransform is explicitly detectable and must fail closed for terminal pixel addressing.
candidates: No a_gt metadata override terminal mutation

terminal_policy.geotransform: six coefficients serialized at full precision
terminal_policy.pixel_anchor: GDAL area-model upper-left corner; pixel center is +0.5,+0.5
terminal_policy.inverse: must be invertible and forward/inverse replay must agree
terminal_policy.rounding: row/col floor or window rounding policy explicitly pinned; no implicit round/ceil substitution
terminal_policy.edges: right/bottom raster extent treated as outside pixel index domain
terminal_policy.pixelispoint: half-pixel semantics audited separately from GDAL area-based geotransform
terminal_policy.windowing: no boundless/outside-source zero fill in terminal path
